newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain enforces copyright law, official says.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain enforces copyright law, official says.

text.p: Bahrain is strictly enforcing a copyright law and has closed some video shops which violated its regulations, a Bahraini official said on Tuesday.
"The law is being strongly enforced in Bahrain," Assistant Undersecretary for Culture and National Heritage Abdullah Yateem told Reuters.
"We have tried and warned some video shop violators recently after giving them a grace period of between three months and one year to correct the situation. Some licences have also been cancelled."
Bahrain's copyright law was issued in 1993 under an Emiri decree. The Cabinet Affairs and Information Ministry enforces the law in cooperation with the Commerce Ministry.
"There are no underground companies in Bahrain that produce pirated cassettes," Yateem said, adding officials regularly raid video stores and other shops to enforce the law.
The Motion Picture Association of the United States claims it lost an estimated $30 million in Bahrain in 1995 to pirated products. It put the country's piracy level then at 100 percent.
The Business Software Alliance, a watchdog for the computer software industry, said in May Bahrain had a piracy rate of 90 percent with estimated revenue losses of $4.5 million.
